findings.body: New `ZADD`, `ZCARD`, and `ZSCAN` commands against old Redis SET keys—and old `SADD` commands against new ZSET keys—fail with `WRONGTYPE`, interrupting span ingestion and flushing until affected keys expire.
findings.failure_mode: Mixed-version or residual buffer state cannot be read or updated by the deployed code.
findings.impact: New `ZADD`, `ZCARD`, and `ZSCAN` commands against old Redis SET keys—and old `SADD` commands against new ZSET keys—fail with `WRONGTYPE`, interrupting span ingestion and flushing until affected keys expire.
findings.root_cause: The patch changes the Redis data type in place without migrating or versioning keys that survive deployments for up to the configured TTL.

findings.title: Changing live span keys from sets to sorted sets is not rollout-compatible

validated_findings.body: `item.datetime` is a `datetime`, so `math.floor` or `math.ceil` raises `TypeError` while building the response cursors and the endpoint returns a 500 response.
validated_findings.evidence: return int(math.floor(value) if self._is_asc(for_prev) else math.ceil(value))
validated_findings.failure_mode: Every non-empty first page through the new optimized branch fails while constructing cursor metadata.
validated_findings.impact: `item.datetime` is a `datetime`, so `math.floor` or `math.ceil` raises `TypeError` while building the response cursors and the endpoint returns a 500 response.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new paginator implements the numeric `Paginator` key logic even though its only caller orders by a `DateTimeField`.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Make this paginator inherit the datetime cursor conversion from `DateTimePaginator`, or implement equivalent timestamp conversion before rounding.
validated_findings.title: Optimized audit-log pagination calls numeric rounding on a datetime
validated_findings.trigger: An authorized user requests `optimized_pagination=true` for an organization with at least one audit-log entry.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 840 exists verbatim in patch. OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/ceil on getattr(item, self.key). AuditLogEntry.datetime is a DateTimeField (confirmed in model L69), so math.floor(datetime) raises TypeError. Trigger is realistic: optimized_pagination=true with audit logs.

validated_findings.body: `build_queryset` passes the numeric cursor value to a `DateTimeField` comparison, causing Django field preparation to fail instead of returning the requested page.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Cursor-based requests fail before the audit-log queryset can be evaluated.
validated_findings.impact: `build_queryset` passes the numeric cursor value to a `DateTimeField` comparison, causing Django field preparation to fail instead of returning the requested page.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new paginator treats a serialized datetime cursor as a value directly comparable to the model's `datetime` field.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Convert the cursor value with the same millisecond-to-timezone-aware-datetime logic used by `DateTimePaginator.value_from_cursor`.
validated_findings.title: Optimized audit-log cursors are not converted back to datetimes
validated_findings.trigger: An authorized audit-log request enables optimized pagination and supplies a cursor with a nonzero timestamp value, including a cursor generated by the existing `DateTimePaginator`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Same root cause as candidate 0: OptimizedCursorPaginator lacks datetime-to-timestamp conversion. value_from_cursor returns raw cursor.value which would be a timestamp int, but build_queryset passes it to DateTimeField comparison. However, the TypeError in get_item_key (candidate 0) occurs first on first page, making this a secondary manifestation of same datetime handling defect.

validated_findings.body: Django querysets do not support negative slice bounds and raise `ValueError`; `paginate` does not catch that exception, so the endpoint returns 500 instead of a page.
validated_findings.failure_mode: The exact cursor form advertised as an advanced feature crashes request execution.
validated_findings.impact: Django querysets do not support negative slice bounds and raise `ValueError`; `paginate` does not catch that exception, so the endpoint returns 500 instead of a page.
validated_findings.root_cause: The implementation assumes that Django ORM querysets automatically handle negative slicing.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Do not pass negative bounds to a Django queryset. Reject negative offsets with `BadPaginationError`, or translate the requested reverse traversal into a nonnegative slice and reversed ordering.
validated_findings.title: Negative offsets cause unsupported Django queryset slicing
validated_findings.trigger: An authorized caller sends an optimized cursor whose offset is negative, such as `0:-1:0`, which explicitly enters the new advanced-feature branch.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 882 exists verbatim. When enable_advanced_features=True and cursor.offset<0, code passes negative start_offset to queryset slice. Django querysets raise ValueError on negative slicing. Trigger requires crafted cursor with negative offset and enable_advanced_features=True.

validated_findings.body: The negative offset is silently changed to zero, which can return the boundary row again and produce duplicate or incorrect traversal instead of rejecting the invalid cursor.
validated_findings.evidence: start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset
validated_findings.failure_mode: Malformed client state is accepted and mapped to the wrong page.
validated_findings.impact: The negative offset is silently changed to zero, which can return the boundary row again and produce duplicate or incorrect traversal instead of rejecting the invalid cursor.
validated_findings.root_cause: The patch normalizes an invalid cursor into a different valid cursor instead of validating it.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Validate `offset < 0` and raise `BadPaginationError`; implement reverse navigation through `is_prev` and ordering rather than negative offsets.
validated_findings.title: Base paginators now silently clamp malformed forward cursors
validated_findings.trigger: Any endpoint using `BasePaginator` receives a tampered forward cursor with a negative offset and a boundary value.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 182 shows max(0, offset) for forward cursors, which clamps negative to zero. This is defensive behavior, not a bug. The claim of 'duplicate rows' is speculative - clamping to 0 simply starts from beginning. No concrete evidence this causes incorrect results vs rejecting invalid input.

validated_findings.body: The value bypasses serializer validation and silently selects the legacy branch; the parameter is also absent from the endpoint's declared query-parameter contract.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Clients receive branch behavior that depends on an undocumented, case-sensitive string comparison rather than validated boolean semantics.
validated_findings.impact: The value bypasses serializer validation and silently selects the legacy branch; the parameter is also absent from the endpoint's declared query-parameter contract.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new public query parameter is parsed manually rather than through the serializer used for every other parameter on the endpoint.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add `optimized_pagination = serializers.BooleanField(required=False, default=False)` to `AuditLogQueryParamSerializer` and read it from `validated_data`.
validated_findings.title: The new query parameter bypasses the endpoint's query serializer
validated_findings.trigger: A client supplies a normal boolean spelling such as `optimized_pagination=True`, `1`, or an invalid value.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 70 exists. While the parameter bypasses serializer validation, this is a stylistic/API design concern rather than a functional bug. The code works correctly for 'true' string. Other values simply don't enable the feature. Low severity design choice, not a defect.

validated_findings.body: New `ZADD`, `ZCARD`, and `ZSCAN` commands against old Redis SET keys—and old `SADD` commands against new ZSET keys—fail with `WRONGTYPE`, interrupting span ingestion and flushing until affected keys expire.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Mixed-version or residual buffer state cannot be read or updated by the deployed code.
validated_findings.impact: New `ZADD`, `ZCARD`, and `ZSCAN` commands against old Redis SET keys—and old `SADD` commands against new ZSET keys—fail with `WRONGTYPE`, interrupting span ingestion and flushing until affected keys expire.
validated_findings.root_cause: The patch changes the Redis data type in place without migrating or versioning keys that survive deployments for up to the configured TTL.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Version the Redis key namespace and provide a controlled transition or dual-read path; do not reuse live SET key names for a different Redis data type.
validated_findings.title: Changing live span keys from sets to sorted sets is not rollout-compatible
validated_findings.trigger: The new consumer is deployed while `span-buf:s:*` keys created by the previous version still exist, or old and new consumers overlap during a rolling deployment.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 197 shows p.zadd replacing p.sadd. During rolling deployment or with existing SET keys from prior version, ZADD against SET key causes WRONGTYPE error. Redis key names unchanged (span-buf:s:*), so type conflict is real during transition.

validated_findings.body: Redis uses `AGGREGATE SUM` by default, so the duplicate payload's timestamp score is multiplied. Eviction then treats that replayed span as artificially newer and removes a different span.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Duplicate delivery silently corrupts retention ordering and changes which payloads survive the 1000-span cap.
validated_findings.impact: Redis uses `AGGREGATE SUM` by default, so the duplicate payload's timestamp score is multiplied. Eviction then treats that replayed span as artificially newer and removes a different span.
validated_findings.root_cause: Set union was replaced with sorted-set union without specifying an idempotent score aggregation mode.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Use `AGGREGATE MAX` for both new `ZUNIONSTORE` calls so merging remains idempotent while preserving the timestamp score.
validated_findings.title: ZUNIONSTORE sums duplicate timestamp scores
validated_findings.trigger: A replayed span payload already exists in the destination segment and is merged again from a child or parent key, which is realistic under at-least-once Kafka delivery.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 47 shows zunionstore without AGGREGATE option. Redis default is SUM. If same payload exists in both keys (at-least-once delivery), scores are summed, corrupting timestamp-based ordering. This affects eviction correctness.

validated_findings.body: Resolution stops before the actual segment root, so subsequent spans are stored and queued under an intermediate key and the trace can be flushed as multiple incorrect segments.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Deep parent chains are only partially joined.
validated_findings.impact: Resolution stops before the actual segment root, so subsequent spans are stored and queued under an intermediate key and the trace can be flushed as multiple incorrect segments.
validated_findings.root_cause: The patch lowers the redirect traversal ceiling from 10000 to 1000 without ensuring redirect chains cannot exceed the new bound.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Retain the previous traversal bound or perform redirect/path compression so the true root is reached without an arbitrary 1000-level correctness limit.
validated_findings.title: The reduced redirect limit splits sufficiently deep segment trees
validated_findings.trigger: A trace has a redirect chain deeper than 1000 entries, such as a deeply nested trace or a long-lived trace whose redirect mappings remain in Redis.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 30 shows loop limit reduced from 10000 to 1000. However, redirect chains of >1000 depth are extremely unlikely in practice. The original comment acknowledged this was theoretical. No evidence such deep chains occur in production.

validated_findings.body: The root payload is removed, but the later `is_root_span` processing still marks the segment as having a root and schedules the short root timeout. Flushing emits a segment whose declared root span is absent.
validated_findings.failure_mode: A trace known to contain its root is flushed without that root and with incomplete segment data.
validated_findings.impact: The root payload is removed, but the later `is_root_span` processing still marks the segment as having a root and schedules the short root timeout. Flushing emits a segment whose declared root span is absent.
validated_findings.root_cause: The eviction policy ranks every payload solely by timestamp and does not reserve the structurally required segment root.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Make root membership identifiable during trimming and exclude it from `ZPOPMIN`; pass the root payload/member information to the script or trim only explicitly non-root members.
validated_findings.title: Eviction can remove the segment's root span
validated_findings.trigger: A segment exceeds 1000 members and its root has one of the lowest end timestamps, or shares a tied score and sorts first by member bytes. The batch writes all payloads before any per-span script runs.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Lines 62-63 show zpopmin evicts lowest-score spans. Root span could have lowest timestamp and be evicted. has_root_span flag (line 67) is set before eviction check, so segment marked as having root but root payload removed. Impact is data corruption.

validated_findings.body: The public constructor setting has no effect: configurations below 1000 retain too many spans, while configurations above 1000 lose spans prematurely.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Runtime behavior disagrees with the instantiated buffer configuration.
validated_findings.impact: The public constructor setting has no effect: configurations below 1000 retain too many spans, while configurations above 1000 lose spans prematurely.
validated_findings.root_cause: The configurable Python limit was disconnected from enforcement and replaced with a Lua literal.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Pass the configured maximum to the Lua script as an argument and use it for trimming, or remove the constructor parameter and migrate every caller to one explicitly documented constant.
validated_findings.title: The configured maximum span count is no longer honored
validated_findings.trigger: `SpansBuffer` is instantiated with `max_segment_spans` set to any value other than the new hard-coded value of 1000.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 62 hardcodes 1000 limit. SpansBuffer constructor accepts max_segment_spans (L150) but Lua script ignores it. The Python parameter has no effect on actual enforcement.

validated_findings.body: The flusher can load and emit an arbitrarily oversized segment because the independent defensive count check has been removed.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Concurrent or interrupted execution bypasses the intended maximum and allows oversized output and memory use.
validated_findings.impact: The flusher can load and emit an arbitrarily oversized segment because the independent defensive count check has been removed.
validated_findings.root_cause: The patch assumes Lua trimming always precedes every possible read despite insertion and trimming occurring in separate nontransactional pipelines.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Retain a load-time span-count check while adapting it to `ZSCAN`, or make insertion, trimming, and queue deadline updates atomic in one Redis script.
validated_findings.title: Removing the load-time count guard leaves a two-phase insertion race unprotected
validated_findings.trigger: A segment is already due for flushing while `process_spans` has completed its nontransactional bulk `ZADD` but has not yet run the Lua trimming pipeline, or the process dies between those phases.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Candidate cites LEFT side line 447 which is removed code. The claim is about removing a defensive check, but the new code relies on Lua-side trimming. The race condition described is speculative without evidence of actual concurrent execution patterns causing oversized segments.
